diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Israel Katz, Israel's Defense Minister, referred to the killing of Samir Abu Yunis, a senior commander of Hamas's military wing, stating that Israel continues to eliminate Hamas leaders in Gaza. He emphasized that the aggressive policy will continue until Gaza is demilitarized and Hamas is destroyed.

Bahrain TV reported early Sunday that the country's air defense systems intercepted and destroyed an Iranian drone. The Ministry of Interior of Bahrain warned about a possible threat and urged citizens to remain calm and go to the nearest safe place.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, dismissed 9 officials after reviewing the findings of the investigation committee on oil smuggling in Jurf al-Nasr and ordered the suspects to be referred to the judiciary. The investigation committee reported the existence of unauthorized refineries and manipulations related to oil smuggling. Intelligence documents show satellite images of crude oil and petroleum products smuggling by an armed group in Jurf al-Nasr, and the investigation committee confirmed the accuracy of this information.

Paris and several other cities in France witnessed street protests for the fifth consecutive Thursday. The Yellow Vests protested against rising prices, labor unions demanded wage increases, and students protested the state of educational facilities.

Aydin Panahi, a member of the executive team of the Iran Prosperity project, emphasized the necessity of evaluating and rebuilding South Pars due to challenges in restoring war-damaged capacities and structural energy imbalances. He said domestic energy security and export development must proceed simultaneously, and oil and gas revenues should be transparent and auditable. Panahi added that rebuilding the energy industry is not possible without the participation of engineers, workers, and active managers in the industry.

France 24 news network, in an investigative report, examined evidence of the presence of proxy forces of the Islamic Republic, including members of the Fatemiyoun Division, in Zahedan and addressed the possible role of these forces in the security developments of Sistan and Baluchestan.

Ali Ehsassi, a member of the Canadian Parliament, described Canada's recent position on the three islands as lacking legal validity and motivated by political reasons. He said Western countries' support for the UAE's claim over these islands is a tool to exert political pressure on the Islamic Republic.

The White House announced that Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping will meet on Thursday, 28 Aban, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China. Kambiz Tavana explains whether Beijing and Moscow will defend the Islamic Republic or if Tehran will turn into possible agreements.

Bourgan Nezami, an economist, said that transporting goods via land routes and third countries like Pakistan and Iraq cannot compensate for the shortage of maritime imports. He emphasized that limited foreign currency resources and a decline in raw material imports have reduced factories' production capacity and intensified inflation.

The 49th ASEAN summit begins in Manila with representatives from 11 member countries. The consequences of the Iran war, rising energy costs, and concerns about oil supply are key topics of this summit.

Fars News Agency reported that the IRGC planned and executed successful attacks on the US base in Bahrain in response to American enemy actions. Bahrain's Ministry of Interior issued a "danger" warning urging people to remain calm and go to the nearest safe place. These warnings were repeated several times early Sunday local time.

Multiple messages report earthquakes in east and northeast Tehran, especially in Narmak, Hakimiyeh, Tehran No, Lavasan, and Pasdaran areas between 7:28 and 7:32. The intensity of the quakes varied, with some described as strong tremors. These reports were received simultaneously from various sources.

Iranian media reported that the death toll in the overturning of a bus on the Dasht Abbas route from Dehloran to Mormori Abdanan on Saturday night reached 12 people. The incident occurred on the evening of Saturday, 23 Aban, and according to the latest report, 15 people were also injured. Also, on the morning of Sunday, 24 Aban, the governor of Ilam announced a special order from Masoud Pezeshkian and the Minister of Interior to investigate the dimensions of this incident.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said on Sunday, 24 Aban, in a pre-session speech that the unveiling of a missile city symbolizes a change in strategic equations in the region. He said regarding the possibility of negotiation or war with the US that if Iran's seven conditions are accepted, the path to agreement is open, and warned that if the Americans make a mistake, the geography of the battle will be determined by Iran's armed forces. Ghalibaf emphasized that the Islamic Republic will not remain in a state of "neither war nor peace."

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said that repeated comments about gasoline have caused public concern. He emphasized that the gasoline problem and energy imbalance should be resolved through expert decisions, collective wisdom, and public cooperation, and that any decision should impose the least pressure on people. Ghalibaf asked officials to refrain from continuous comments about gasoline and called for market improvement through supervision and urgent plans.
A video received by Iran International shows a long line of cars on the Bushehr-Choghadak ring road in front of a fuel station.

The Bahrain Defense Force Command announced that the Islamic Republic continues its systematic hostile actions through overt attacks against targets in the Kingdom of Bahrain. The command stated that Bahrain's air defense systems intercepted and destroyed several drone attacks from Tehran before they reached their targets. It also emphasized that all military units and weapons in Bahrain are at the highest level of readiness and are fully prepared to defend Bahrain.

It was reported that Galaleh (Nazanin) Elyasi, a citizen from Mahabad, appeared at the Enforcement Branch of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of the county on Saturday, 23 Aban. She was arrested to serve a two-year prison sentence and transferred to Urmia prison.

On 24 Aban, long queues for gasoline were reported in Bushehr, Yasuj, and Shiraz. The price of a tank of gasoline in Yasuj reached 4 million tomans, and people are unhappy with the queues and reduced gasoline quotas. It was also reported that plainclothes forces appeared in Shiraz and Marvdasht, and the atmosphere in the area is tense.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, called the Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General's request for compensation from Iran unfounded and said Tehran will seriously pursue compensation from regional countries. Baqaei added that the support of regional countries for Saddam Hussein's regime during the war with Iran has not been forgotten, and some countries provided Iraq with hundreds of billions of dollars in financial, military, and armament aid. He also said that regional countries participated in attacks by providing their airspace, waters, and land to the enemy, and the Islamic Republic has documented their role.
It was reported that a bus carrying workers of the Dehloran gas refinery overturned on the Abdanan route, injuring 16 workers and causing the death of 12 others.
Yesterday, a man in a village in Jahrom County killed his wife and mother-in-law due to family disputes using a cold weapon. The suspect was arrested by law enforcement officers.

Persepolis club referred its complaint against Yaser Asani, the Albanian winger of Esteghlal, to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) for international review of the player's contract case. Persepolis believes that Asani's contract with Esteghlal was terminated and re-signed before the season started while the club's transfer window was closed. Persepolis considers this action contrary to transfer regulations and is continuing legal proceedings at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
According to a video received by Iran International, cars in Nourabad Mamasani formed a long queue in front of a fuel station on the evening of Saturday, 23 Aban to receive gasoline.

Ahmad Rastineh, spokesperson for the National Defense and Power faction of the parliament, said that Iran has approached absolute deterrence thresholds and this deterrence can be displayed against any miscalculation by the US in using unconventional weapons. He added that in case of a US atomic attack on some areas of the country, this absolute deterrence will be extensively demonstrated. He also stated that Iran's nuclear technology is far more advanced compared to Israel and Pakistan.

Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United captain, has decided to postpone contract extension negotiations until the performance of Mauricio Pochettino, the new coach, becomes clear. The 32-year-old Fernandes has rejected two contract extension offers so far and intends to evaluate the team's situation under Pochettino. He is unhappy with the team's poor results and some management decisions and wants to see if the club properly supports Pochettino.

Romário, former Brazil national team striker and 1994 World Cup champion, strongly criticized Carlo Ancelotti after Brazil's 3-2 friendly loss to Japan and called for his immediate dismissal. He asked the president of the Brazilian Football Confederation to remove Ancelotti before the national team enters a deeper crisis. Romário emphasized that Ancelotti has been successful at club level but has not achieved results with the Brazil national team.

The head of the Kidney Patients Support Association in Kermanshah province reported the absence of a dialysis unit in Kerend-e Gharb and stated that dialysis patients must visit medical centers in Eslamabad-e Gharb three days a week. Hossein Biglari said that the request for transportation services for these patients has so far been unsuccessful. Due to their physical condition and difficulty using public transport, patients are forced to use internet taxis and private cars at their own expense, which has become a serious concern for them.

It was reported that in Iranian schools, two months after the start of the academic year, heating equipment is still not provided and students have to stay in the cold schoolyard. Problems such as lack of good teachers, power outages, and social pressures on students and teachers were also reported. Some students and teachers criticized the difficult conditions and lack of resources.

It was reported by Students United that the security of Alzahra University summoned several students in recent days who had passed through the dormitory gate with Halloween makeup. According to this report, the university security identified these students after several weeks by reviewing CCTV footage and subjected them to repression and disciplinary actions due to their Halloween makeup. The summoned students also faced reproachful statements during these confrontations and were required to provide written commitments.

Hungarian authorities discovered and seized nearly 20 million dollars in cash during investigations into bribery allegations against Miklós Seszták, the former development minister. Part of the money was buried in forests and part hidden in agricultural buildings and warehouses. Seszták denied any wrongdoing, and his lawyer said the seized money does not belong to his client.
A man accused of previously raping a young female student in Damavand was identified in a prison in one of the eastern provinces of the country and was transferred to Tehran province for trial.
A video received by Iran International shows a long line of cars on Sunday, 24 Aban, waiting to get gasoline in the city of Jam, Bushehr province.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, said that the Islamic Republic is once again trying to revive its nuclear program. He emphasized that Israel must prevent the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons through actions similar to the "Lion's Awakening" and "Lion's Roar" operations.
A defendant in Karaj was sentenced to 74 lashes and other punishments by Branch Six of the Alborz Province Court of Appeals.

Houshang Hasan-Yari, a Middle East and military affairs expert, said the IRGC attacks on Bahrain have discredited mediators' efforts to reduce tensions. He added that the Islamic Republic, by increasing drone attacks and military actions against regional countries and ships, aims to deter the US from war and force Washington to leave the region. According to him, this strategy could push the US into the final stage of war.

Abbas Golrou, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said it is in the interest of the US and its allies to stop the current process and avoid military confrontation, as the reaction of the Islamic Republic could be deterrent and proportionate to the circumstances. He added that the scope of the war could expand and new objectives have been defined in the same geography. Golrou also stated that the armed forces of the Islamic Republic are at a high level of readiness.

Masoud Pezeshkian said at the "Book and Reading Day" meeting on Sunday, 24 Aban that reading books is very important for managers and officials to better understand the conditions and daily life of society. He added that managers should read books that help them provide better service and solve people's problems. Pezeshkian emphasized that to solve people's problems, one must see what predecessors who solved problems did and adapt oneself to those experiences.

Ata Hosseinian, an economic and energy journalist, said that the Islamic Republic, simultaneously with implementing the gasoline consumer identification plan in Tehran, has also limited gasoline supply in border provinces through rationing and drip-feed distribution. He described these measures as signs of gasoline shortage and a gap between production and consumption, adding that the government is trying to prepare for a gasoline price increase and budget deficit compensation by limiting supply.
A video sent to Iran International shows a student releasing white balloons in front of the Faculty of Engineering in Tehran in memory of those killed in Aban 98.
"Hamed Deldar" was wounded by three bullets in the Rasht protests on 18 Dey and died two days later. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Today, Sunday, a group of retired steel industry workers held a protest gathering and march in front of the Isfahan governor's office. The protesting retirees demanded the proper implementation of salary equalization, an increase in pensions in line with inflation rates, and resolution of issues related to healthcare services and their pension fund.

Today, Sunday 24 Aban, a number of Social Security retirees held a protest in front of the organization's buildings in the cities of Shush and Kermanshah. Their demands include equalizing pensions, increasing payments in line with living costs, removing the Social Security Organization from government monopoly, resolving supplementary insurance issues, and implementing Article 54 of the Social Security Law for free medical services.

The request for retrial by Koukab Badaghi Pegah, a teacher residing in Izeh, was rejected for the second time by the Supreme Court, and her case was sent to the enforcement branch for the execution of the prison sentence.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic's missile program can also threaten NATO European countries. He added that the Islamic Republic is using a hybrid warfare strategy to increase the cost of military confrontation for the US and Europe. Aghaei emphasized that the Islamic Republic is effectively conducting a hybrid war against the US, Europe, and regional countries.

Tasnim News Agency reported that the new three-year contract of Alireza Beiranvand with Tractor Club, despite being officially announced a month ago, still lacks the signature of the then CEO and its validity is uncertain. The name of Hojat Karimi is on the contract as CEO, but with his resignation, the club must draft a new contract signed by the new CEO. Beiranvand is currently serving his military duty at Fajr Sepasi Club, and Tractor must reach a new agreement with him to sign the new contract.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, responded to the International Atomic Energy Agency's request to inspect Iran's nuclear facilities by saying they will not allow inspectors to enter until they are sure their behavior and speech have been corrected. He also questioned whether the inspectors are honest employees of the agency or spies for Israel and the US. These remarks were made on Sunday, 24 Aban.

A video received by Iran International shows that a group of drivers at Kermanshah cargo terminal on Sunday, 24 Aban stopped work and went on strike due to lack of oil and what they call unfair distribution.

Hassan Qashqavi, spokesperson for the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the diplomatic path is not closed but the Islamic Republic has announced its "seven conditions" and is now in the "post-negotiation phase." He added that the Islamic Republic is in the "post-agreement and post-negotiation era" and there is no longer any subject for dialogue. Qashqavi also referred to previous negotiations with the US and said that an agreement was signed but the American side did not adhere to it.
Today, a number of truck drivers in Rafsanjan held a protest gathering in front of the office of the Friday Imam of the city against the reduction of their fuel quota.
According to a video received by Iran International, cars in the city of Gerash in Fars province formed a long queue in front of a gas station on Sunday, 24 Aban, to receive gasoline.

Videos received by Iran International show severe violence by police officers during the arrest of individuals in the Malashieh neighborhood of Ahvaz on Sunday, 24 Aban. According to reports, officers entered the neighborhood to collect illegal electricity and arrested several people with shooting and severe beatings.

A group of protesters gathered on Saturday, 23 Aban, in Borujerd in front of Fatemeh Maqsoudi's office, the representative of Borujerd in the parliament, and threw mud at the office door. The protesters said they have paid the amounts related to land allocation since 1382 but the status of the lands has not been determined after more than two decades. They criticized the fruitlessness of follow-ups and demanded serious intervention by officials and a swift resolution of their demands.

On Sunday, 24 Aban, Qatar's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the continuation of attacks by the Islamic Republic on Bahrain and called it a clear violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of that country. The ministry stated these attacks are a blatant violation of international laws, the UN Charter, and principles of good neighborliness. Qatar warned that the continuation of these attacks creates a dangerous escalation that could complicate efforts to contain regional tensions.

Today, Sunday, a number of private and taxi drivers passing through Minab gathered in front of the county governor's office. These individuals gathered after seeking to receive the allocated 20-liter gasoline quota from the Minab governor's office. The protesting citizens demand an increase in the gasoline quota and improvements in its distribution method.

A UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 passenger plane collided on the evening of Saturday, 23 Aban at Miami International Airport. Two people suffered minor injuries and were treated on site without needing hospital transfer. The incident did not affect airport operations.

Harana News Agency reported that Hossein Savari, Saeed Savari, Ebrahim Savari, Hamood Savari, and Khalil Savari, five unemployed youths from Howeyzeh county, were arrested following a protest gathering in front of Dana Sohrab Oil Company on Saturday, 23 Aban. The gathering was held to protest employment conditions and to demand job opportunities. The detainees are aged between 25 and 30 years.

For the third time in 24 hours, an earthquake has shaken the Lavasan area in northeastern Tehran. The Seismology Organization of the University of Tehran reported the magnitude of this earthquake as 3. Reports indicate multiple tremors in various parts of Tehran including Narmak, Hakimiyeh, and Tehranpars.

The court session addressing the charges against Morteza Nemati, a PhD graduate in Geography from the University of Tehran, was held on Saturday, 23 Aban, at the Abdanan Revolutionary Court. In this session, Morteza Nemati defended himself against the charge of "propaganda against the regime." This report was published by Harana News Agency.

With the ongoing economic crisis in Iran and the increasing difficulty of providing for households, the sale of women's hair has significantly increased. Reviewing advertisements and sellers' accounts shows that covering education, medical, essential purchases, and family expenses are among the main motivations for selling hair. An interview with Sharareh Azizi, a member of Iran International's editorial team.
Following cyberattacks and threats attributed to the Islamic Republic, The New York Times reported that security alerts in Europe have sharply increased.

The broadcast of the series "Yal" was stopped by order of the Tehran Culture and Media Prosecutor's Office due to what was described as "the dissemination of criminal content contrary to public decency and ethics."

Mehdi Taj, head of the Iranian Football Federation, stated that due to sanctions, it is not possible to receive financial resources from FIFA and the Asian Football Confederation, and they plan to meet with FIFA officials to find a solution. Taj said FIFA informed them in a letter that due to sanctions, it cannot pay money for building the new football federation building. He added that the ticket cost per person for attending the Asian Beach Soccer Championship in Thailand is one billion tomans.
Videos released show that a group of retired steelworkers in Isfahan gathered on Sunday, 24 Aban, to pursue their livelihood issues.
Diyar Haji Rasulpour, a citizen from Bukan, was transferred to the prison of this city to serve a six-month prison sentence.
Including the arrests of Hasan Qorqchi and Masoud Qorqchi, the number of detainees on Saturday, 23 Aban in Boukan reached four individuals.

Sirus Ahmadi, Director General of the Office of Sports Clubs at the Ministry of Sports, stated that Persepolis's debt for hosting matches, calculated with the Central Bank index, has exceeded 350 billion tomans. He said this amount has been owed to the Development Company from 2013 until before the start of Azadi Stadium's renovation. Ahmadi also criticized Persepolis for making unilateral demands from the government and urged them to use existing capacities instead.

Teresa Lazaro, the Philippine Foreign Minister, said this action has affected all ASEAN member countries. She addressed the consequences of the Iran war on energy security, food security, and rising oil prices at the ASEAN summit press conference in Manila. Lazaro also reported that more than two million five hundred thousand Filipino nationals reside in the countries bordering the Persian Gulf.

Fariba Asadi, a civil activist linked to the 1404 protests, was sentenced to six years of imprisonment and additional penalties. According to Harana News Agency, she was convicted of charges including assembly and collusion, acting against national security, and participating in protests. The court also imposed additional penalties of two years of travel ban, prohibition from membership in social groups, and dismissal from government and public jobs.

The Ynet website reported that despite repeated statements by the Islamic Republic about oil tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, the assessment is that the vessels are actually targeted by direct attacks from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Ashkan Safaei, an Iran International reporter, reports.

Reports from Dezful, Tehran, Damghan, and Lorestan describe economic hardships. A soldier with a 22 million toman salary complains about corruption among commanders, and a university faculty member with a 45 million toman salary says they run out of money by the tenth of the month. Additionally, issues such as increased car repair costs, expensive tires, salary cuts for staff, poor bakery conditions, and unpaid wages for Tehran bus company employees have been reported.

In the early morning of Sunday, 24 Aban, the death sentence of a female prisoner named Fatemeh Farhadi was carried out in Adel Abad Prison in Shiraz. This prisoner had previously been sentenced to death on non-political charges. The news was reported by HRANA news agency.
A video sent to Iran International shows severe air pollution in Tehran on Sunday, 24 Aban.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, said the goal of the plan to amend the appointment conditions of the Minister of Intelligence is not to remove the requirement of Ijtihad but to provide the opportunity to use specialized forces. He added that having Ijtihad is an advantage for those with years of expert activity in the Ministry of Intelligence, but choosing someone outside this body who only has the Ijtihad condition and lacks intelligence knowledge and experience cannot be useful for the security apparatus. Azizi emphasized that the plan is still under review and expert proposals will be received in the coming days.

Ahmad Bugari, Deputy of Culture and Education at the General Directorate of Education in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, announced that schools in this province face a shortage of counselors. According to Bugari, schools in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari need about 800 counselors, but currently about 200 counselors are working in these schools.

Kata'ib Hezbollah Iraq stated that despite entering negotiations and signing an agreement on national sovereignty, it will not relinquish its weapons and will not retreat in the face of pressure from the US, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. The group accused the Iraqi government of not adhering to its commitments and using pressure tactics and fabricated cases. It also denied allegations of oil smuggling in the city of Nasr and said a technical committee found no interference with oil pipelines.
A video received by Iran International shows a schoolgirl putting up a photo of a young Prince Reza Pahlavi in the classroom.

Yousef Akbari, head of pre-hospital emergency services in Qazvin, announced that over 50% of the province's ambulances are worn out and need replacement. He said the existing fleet does not meet the province's needs, and the shortage of suitable ambulances in mountainous areas has caused service difficulties. He also mentioned that the lack of hospital facilities in some areas has increased the need to transfer patients to other centers.

Arsène Wenger, former Arsenal coach and FIFA's global football development director, decided not to run in the FIFA presidential election and not to compete against Gianni Infantino. This decision came after considering candidacy and amid opposition faced by Infantino. UEFA is still seeking to introduce another candidate before the registration deadline.
It was reported that a sound similar to a missile launch was heard in Qeshm. It was said that a missile passed by.

The United Students channel reported that in recent months at least 20 students of the Farabi Faculties at the University of Tehran have faced disciplinary actions and their cases have been referred to the disciplinary committee. Additionally, three other students were arrested and are now released, but their legal cases are still ongoing in court. The channel also reported the presence and influence of security institutions and Basij forces within the internal environment of the Farabi Faculties at the University of Tehran.
Videos received show that students of Yazd University on Sunday, 24 Aban, protested the poor quality of the university cafeteria food by throwing their food trays on the ground.

The UK Maritime Trade Center announced that an oil tanker was attacked while moving east in the Persian Gulf, before entering the Strait of Hormuz. All crew members are safe, but the extent of damage and potential environmental consequences are still unknown. The center also reported that in the past 72 hours, one attack on ships in the Persian Gulf was recorded, and activities by the Revolutionary Guard against commercial ships continue.

Atousa Babadi, a citizen from Sabzevar, has been detained by the Sabzevar Intelligence Department forces since 13 Aban and remains in the city's prison. According to Harana News Agency, she was transferred to prison after two days in the intelligence detention center.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, compared senior officials of the Islamic Republic to "rats in a sewer pipe" and said they are in underground shelters unaware of the worsening situation on the surface. He added that the officials are completely isolated and flight restrictions have eliminated their ability to travel to European countries.
A video received by Iran International shows mazut burning at Arak power plant and air pollution on Sunday, 24 Aban.

Omid Shams, a legal expert and international affairs analyst, said that intelligence agencies of the Islamic Republic use meetings of supporters of the Islamic Republic and anti-Semitic activists in Britain to identify, recruit, and employ their agents. He added that the Islamic Republic exploits the freedoms in democratic societies as a platform to infiltrate these communities and advance anti-Semitic and terrorist activities.
A video sent to Iran International from Iranshahr in Sistan and Baluchestan province shows a long line of vehicles waiting for fuel at 4:30 AM on Sunday, 24 Aban.

Miad Maleki, former head of the Targeting Office of the US Treasury Department, said about Mossad's warning to Washington regarding the Islamic Republic's plan to target Donald Trump and senior officials of his administration: "These threats make the US government more determined to increase pressure on the Islamic Republic, and Trump will finish the Islamic Republic's work in the next two years."

The Islamic Republic's renewed attack on Bahrain has faced regional condemnation. Qatar's Foreign Ministry described the attack as a factor weakening diplomatic efforts. The Wall Street Journal reported that US intelligence agencies estimate the Islamic Republic has between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles, which would provide significant capability to strike American and allied targets if war resumes.

Informed sources told Iran International that prisoners in Ward 4, Unit 6 of Tehran's Great Prison face severe food shortages, unsanitary conditions, and limited access to showers. Many of these prisoners are detainees from the January protests. The population of this ward is estimated to be between 360 and 400 people.

In recent years, reports have emerged about the assassination, kidnapping, and interrogation of IRGC members by Mossad. The New York Times, in an investigative report, covered Mossad and the Israeli government's efforts to clarify the fate of Ron Arad, an Israeli pilot missing since October 1986, and details of the kidnapping of two senior IRGC commanders by Mossad. An interview was conducted with Ashkan Safaei, a reporter for Iran International.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations regarding the non-use of children in military affairs, 1,281 students from various counties were sent to operational areas as part of the Rahian-e Noor tours. Also, an official from the Ministry of Education announced that this year, 250,000 students from across the country will be sent to operational areas in the south and northwest of the country with the participation of the Ministry of Education and the Student Basij Organization.

Nazanin Abedini, a Baháʼí citizen residing in Qaemshahr, was sentenced by the Sari Revolutionary Court to three years in prison and eight years of deprivation of social rights. She was charged with propaganda against the Islamic Republic system and propaganda in favor of groups opposing the system. The court considered her educational and religious activities, including teaching Baháʼí beliefs to children, as falling under Article 500 bis of the Islamic Penal Code and issued her sentence accordingly.

Abbas Mousavi, acting deputy of the political office of the presidency, stated that Mostafa Pourmohammadi is among the government's candidates for the Ministry of Intelligence and that the selection requires consensus. He mentioned that some names like Mohammad Sadegh Motamedian and Alireza Rashidian might not be considered by government committees. Mousavi described the Ministry of Intelligence as sensitive and emphasized it must be managed without factional disputes.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said the Islamic Consultative Assembly, by approving an urgent plan to reform the structure of the Ministry of Intelligence, seeks to reduce the government's powers and increase Mojtaba Khamenei's direct control over intelligence institutions. According to this plan, two organizations of Information Protection and Political-Ideological will be formed, whose heads will be directly appointed by the Supreme Leader. These organizations, by supervising the performance of the minister and employees of the Ministry of Intelligence, will weaken the minister's position and transfer control of the ministry from the government to the Supreme Leader.

At least 9 protest gatherings were held on Sunday, 24 Aban. Truck drivers in Rafsanjan protested in front of the city’s Friday Imam office. Social Security retirees also gathered in several cities including Shush, Rasht, Kermanshah, Tehran, and Ahvaz.
A man in Tehran accused of killing his wife and 12-year-old daughter was tried today in Branch 10 of the criminal court of this province.

Three days after Trump said he no longer wants an agreement with the Islamic Republic, Qalibaf warned that Tehran will not accept a state of neither war nor peace. An hour ago, the IRGC attacked Bahrain with a drone; a step towards a preemptive attack, while Netanyahu has called for an immediate attack on Iran.

Nejat Bahrami said the Islamic Republic's renewed attack on Bahrain is an attempt to exit the state of neither war nor peace and to end pressures from the American blockade. He added that Tehran aims to increase tensions by targeting regional infrastructure and push the US to start a new round of war. Bahrami believes that continued missile attacks and increased US military readiness will make a broad conflict inevitable.

Marca reported that the match between Ravenna and Forlì, the Emilia-Romagna derby, became the most viewed match in the history of Italy's Serie C. The reason for this attention was Ronaldinho's return to professional football, 11 years after retiring. Ronaldinho returned to the pitch on November 15, 2026, at the Bruno Benelli stadium and played for more than half an hour.

Investigations by Iran International show that Hossein Yazdankhah, head of the fifth branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, has played a role in issuing death sentences for several December protesters and sentencing lawyers and political prisoners. He has issued death sentences for at least 11 detainees from the December protests and has been involved in cases such as the conviction of Fatemeh Sepahri and the confiscation of Marzieh Mohabi's assets. Despite this record, his name is not on the individual sanctions lists of the US, UK, or the European Union.
Niusha Saremi reported in the audio version of Titrawol that Mossad warned about Tehran's plan to assassinate Trump. It was also reported that the US and Europe are on security alert.

Videos received by Iran International show a group of Iranians residing in the UK in the cities of London and Sheffield in England and Glasgow in Scotland, taking to the streets against the Islamic Republic.
It was reported that Mojtaba Khamenei took the first step to seize the Ministry of Intelligence.

Leila Morvati, a political analyst, said political and economic monopoly, suppression of protests, and military expenses have caused a deep economic crisis for the Islamic Republic. She added that the government struggles to meet the economic needs of its middle layers and economic decline has surpassed political decline. Morvati also said regional tensions continue and Republican disagreements do not mean the military option is off the table.

Narges Mohammadi, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, criticized the ongoing repression of writers, poets, and journalists in Iran on her Instagram, mentioning arrests, trials, and sentences including death penalties. She referred to the retrial of five journalists and poets in Abadan and the referral of death sentence for imprisoned songwriter Peyman Farahavar to the enforcement branch. Mohammadi also mentioned the treatment of several writers and prison sentences for others, emphasizing the importance of supporting imprisoned writers.

Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst, said the Islamic Republic government is implementing a broad plan to eliminate energy subsidies with a focus on combating fuel smuggling. She added that a large part of fuel smuggling is organized and the cost of combating it falls on the people and drivers. Taherkhani warned that calculating gasoline prices based on dollar rates could greatly increase economic pressure and inflation.

The Iranian Writers' Association reported on the World Day of Imprisoned Writers that at least 20 writers and poets are imprisoned or detained, and one imprisoned writer faces the risk of execution. The association stated that after the suppression of the protests in Dey 1404 and the war of the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic, a climate of intimidation and censorship has prevailed in the country. They also warned about the risk of execution of Peyman Farahavar.

Ghassan Ashour, a Middle East analyst, said the Iraqi government is trying to reduce the influence of armed groups close to the Islamic Republic by pursuing the oil smuggling case in the Jurf al-Sakhar area.
